summary.title: Edit in 2D, Verify in 3D: Reinforcement Learning for Multi-view Consistent Scene Editing

details: Instruction-based 3D scene editing lacks paired multi-view-consistent editing data, making supervised fine-tuning of 2D editors infeasible, while prior attention/depth-warping and per-scene optimization pipelines remain inconsistent, slow, or restricted to geometry-preserving edits.
Key asymmetry exploited: generating multi-view consistent images is hard, but verifying 3D consistency is tractable — so RL with a verifiable reward can substitute for supervision.

RL3DEdit: GRPO-based RL fine-tuning of a multi-image 2D editor (FLUX-Kontext) that jointly edits M rendered views in a single forward pass, using a frozen 3D foundation model (VGGT) as the reward model.

Reward design: VGGT's depth and point confidence maps as multi-view consistency signals, relative-pose (adjacent-view extrinsics) error as viewpoint-alignment signal, plus an 'anchor' reward that swaps one view for a pre-computed high-quality single-view edit and scores it via LPIPS to preserve 2D editing fidelity.
Claim that data-driven 3D-foundation-model rewards resist reward hacking, unlike SfM- or photometric-warping-based verifiers.
FLUX-Kontext-dev fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 32, alpha 32); M=9 evenly sampled views per scene; equal reward weights 0.25 each.
Flow-GRPO-style SDE sampling with noise level 0.8, group size 16, 12 denoising steps (vs 6 in 2D RL work), MixGRPO window size 4; KL penalty to the original editor.
One epoch on a single RTX Pro 6000, 42 hours.
8 scenes from IN2N, BlendedMVS, Mip-NeRF360; 70 VLM-generated (Gemini 2.5) edit prompts across scenes; 1,319 nine-view training samples (~5% of Tinker's ~25K paired samples).
Anchor images: offline single-image FLUX-Kontext edits of all views with light quality filtering (>98% usable).
Test split of 100 cases: 70 novel-view (in-distribution), 16 unseen instructions, 14 new-scene cases (room, stump, fangzhou, kitchen).
Single forward pass produces 9 edited views; 3DGS reconstruction warm-started with AnySplat feed-forward init, then 3,000 iterations of photometric optimization (~40s).
DGE, GaussCtrl, EditSplat (InstructPix2Pix-based), plus a re-implemented EditSplat with FLUX-Kontext backbone for fair comparison.

Metrics: VIEScore (GPT-4.1 VLM judge, newly applied to 3D editing), CLIP directional similarity, photometric reprojection loss (Ph-Loss) with VGGT depth and GT poses, average editing time, and a 25-participant user study on rendered videos.

Reward component removals (r^D+r^P, r^T, r^a); replacing VGGT reward with SfM-based reward or reprojection-warping reward; swapping backbone to Qwen-Image-Edit; anchor selection (fixed vs random), denoising steps (6/12/20), reward weight skews (geometry-heavy vs quality-heavy) — all trained/tested on the face scene split (>200 samples).

key_findings.finding: RL with VGGT-derived geometric rewards yields state-of-the-art 3D editing quality, consistency, and speed in a single pass without per-scene optimization.
key_findings.evidence: VIEScore 5.48 vs 3.23 for the strongest baseline (EditSplat w/ FLUX-Kontext), CLIP-dir 0.147 vs 0.125, lowest Ph-Loss 0.076, and 1.5 min per edit vs 3.5-40 min (>2x faster than InstructPix2Pix pipelines, >20x than the FLUX-based baseline); 71.4% user preference in-distribution and 60.0% zero-shot.

key_findings.finding: VGGT's confidence maps are a reliable, interpretable proxy for multi-view consistency, justifying their use as a reward.
key_findings.evidence: Progressively replacing consistent views with independently edited ones on 100 nine-view sets shows near-linear decay of mean predicted depth confidence; spatially, editing only a background or adding glasses in one view drops confidence precisely in the corresponding regions.

key_findings.finding: Traditional geometry verifiers are trivially reward-hacked whereas the data-driven 3D foundation model reward is not.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing the VGGT reward with an SfM reward collapses to textureless outputs (VIEScore 0.97, Ph-Loss 0.201); the reprojection-warping reward yields the lowest Ph-Loss (0.065) but severely blurred images (VIEScore 1.41), versus 5.26/0.077 for the full model on the same face split.

key_findings.finding: Each reward component is necessary, with the anchor reward specifically preventing RL from collapsing toward over-smoothed low-frequency edits.
key_findings.evidence: Ablations on the face split: without r^D and r^P, VIEScore 2.11 / Ph-Loss 0.193 with visible ghosting; without r^T, 4.77 / 0.131 with subtle viewpoint shifts; without r^a, 4.34 / 0.091 with over-smoothed textures; skewing weights (geometry-heavy 4.31, quality-heavy 3.97) is worse than equal weighting.

key_findings.finding: RL fine-tuning augments rather than reshapes the 2D editor, so its 2D editing ability and generalization are retained.
key_findings.evidence: VIEScore on GEdit-Bench-EN is essentially unchanged before vs after RL; zero-shot performance on 30 unseen-instruction/new-scene cases (VIEScore 5.40) nearly matches in-distribution (5.52) despite baselines being per-scene optimized on those test cases; the framework transfers to Qwen-Image-Edit (5.43 / 0.079).
